sentence: This project studies how gene regulation in the ovary changes during aging and links to genetic factors that affect age at menopause.
This project combines research tools in genetics and genomics with activities led by social scientists to share knowledge with society.
This project tries to find out how blocking part of the complement pathway changes the way tissues and colorectal tumors respond to radiation.
This project tests a light-activated drug delivery treatment for locally advanced pancreatic cancer in mice, rats and rabbits.
This project builds a hub for cancer screening research and joins a feasibility study of multi-cancer early detection screening.
This project builds deep learning methods that analyze whole-body scans of lymphoma taken at several time points.
This project runs a core that offers metabolomics and mitochondrial energetics techniques to researchers studying brain metabolism.
This project tries to make donor heart assessment more data-driven and systematic so more donor hearts can be used for heart transplants.
This project studies how blood stem cells that last a lifetime differ from progenitor cells that form alongside them during embryonic development.
This project develops a gene-editing tool using baculoviral vectors that disrupts genes only in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma cells.
This project looks for genetic factors that change how severe thoracic aortic aneurysm is and builds an echocardiographic image analysis algorithm.
This project tracks how coronavirus replicates and how host cells respond, using single-molecule imaging and computational models in cells and murine models.
This project develops a tumor-specific biomarker agent to detect metastatic breast cancer in the brain and make it more sensitive to radiation therapy.
This project develops probes that detect and analyze post-translational modifications, which are chemical changes to proteins, across whole cells.
This project studies how a protein called osteopontin senses and controls inflammation in the brain, focusing on microglia and neurons in the striatum.
This project uses structural, biophysical and cellular approaches to find out how a receptor tyrosine kinase assembles and becomes activated.
This project develops macrophages carrying a chimeric antigen receptor to fight triple negative breast cancer by targeting a marker on tumor cells.
This project develops a technology that combines fetal magnetocardiography and fetal echocardiography to study the fetal heart.
This project provides electron and light microscopy tools and assays to study cells and tissues in cancer research.
This project coordinates a network of centers working on cancer adoptive cellular therapy, including specimens, data management and trials.
